title: Revealing the Microscopic Pattern of GB’s Effect on Macroscopic Thermal Conductivity
content: Grain boundaries are the interfaces where crystals of different orientations meet within a material, often forming when the material undergoes processes such as solidification or recrystallization. These boundaries play a crucial role in determining the material's overall properties, including its thermal conductivity. In general, grain boundaries can impede the flow of heat by scattering phonons, which are the primary carriers of thermal energy in solids. The presence of grain boundaries reduces the material's ability to efficiently transfer heat, leading to lower thermal conductivity compared to single-crystal materials. The effect of grain boundaries on thermal conductivity is influenced by factors such as grain size, orientation, and the presence of impurities or defects. Smaller grains typically create more boundaries, further restricting thermal transport, while larger grains may allow heat to flow more freely.
